title: Intastellar Accounts — Sign in
description: Web sign-in with Intastellar Accounts on inta.dev — OAuth-style flows, PKCE, redirects, sessions, and security.
text: Intastellar Accounts — Sign in Web sign-in with Intastellar Accounts on inta.dev — OAuth-style flows, PKCE, redirects, sessions, and security. Intastellar Accounts is the identity layer for Intastellar products. This documentation describes how to add web sign in so users can authenticate with the same account they use across Intastellar services. What you will build 1. Send the user to Intastellar to sign in authorization step . 2. Receive them back on your site with a short lived authorization code . 3. Exchange that code for tokens and optionally establish your own session . 4. Keep the session secure in the browser and on your servers. Guides Sign in — Web Getting started /docs/accounts sign in/web/getting started — prerequisites, register an app, pick a flow. Authorization code flow /docs/accounts sign in/web/authorization code flow — auth URL, state , PKCE, and the code exchange. Redirect URIs and callbacks /docs/accounts sign in/web/redirect uris — allowed URLs, validation, and common mistakes. Sessions, cookies, and tokens /docs/accounts sign in/web/sessions and cookies — inta acc , inta state , and storage choices. SPAs and JavaScript clients /docs/accounts sign in/web/spa and javascript — public clients and PKCE in the browser. Server side confidential clients /docs/accounts sign in/web/backend exchange — exchanging the code on your backend. Logout, errors, and troubleshooting /docs/accounts sign in/web/logout and errors — ending sessions and fixing typical issues. Related products Intastellar Consents cookie banner /docs/cookie banner — GDPR consent UI if you also need a cookie banner on the same site. Note on the legacy docs URL Content that was previously published under developers.intastellarsolutions.com/identity/sign in/web/docs https://developers.intastellarsolutions.com/identity/sign in/web/docs is maintained here on inta.dev as the developer platform for Intastellar. Use the guides above as the current reference.

title: Authorization code flow
description: Build the authorize redirect, validate state and PKCE, and exchange the authorization code for tokens with Intastellar Accounts.
text: Authorization code flow Build the authorize redirect, validate state and PKCE, and exchange the authorization code for tokens with Intastellar Accounts. The authorization code flow is the standard pattern for web sign in: the browser visits Intastellar, the user authenticates, and Intastellar redirects back to your site with a code you exchange for tokens. Step 1 — Redirect the user to authorize Send the user’s browser to the authorization endpoint with query parameters names follow common OAuth 2.0 / OIDC conventions; confirm exact names in your console : Parameter Purpose response type Use code for this flow. client id Your registered client ID. redirect uri Must exactly match a registered URI. scope Space separated scopes often includes openid for OIDC . state Random, unguessable value; you verify it on return. code challenge PKCE: SHA 256 hash of code verifier , Base64url encoded for public clients . code challenge method Typically S256 . Example line breaks for readability : Store state and the raw code verifier for PKCE server side or in a secure, short lived cookie so you can validate them on callback. Step 2 — Handle the callback Intastellar redirects to your redirect uri with: Query param Meaning code One time authorization code. state Echo of the value you sent; must match stored state . If the user denies access or an error occurs, you may receive error and error description instead — handle these without treating them as success. Step 3 — Exchange the code for tokens POST to the token endpoint typically application/x www form urlencoded : Field Purpose grant type authorization code code The code from the callback. redirect uri Same URI as in step 1. client id Your client ID. code verifier PKCE: the original secret verifier public clients . client secret Confidential clients only. The response usually includes access token , optional refresh token , and an id token when openid was requested. Validate the ID token issuer, audience, expiry, signature using JWKS from the issuer when you rely on claims in your app. Security checklist Never skip state verification — prevents CSRF on the callback. Use PKCE for any client that cannot hold a client secret SPAs, mobile . Use HTTPS for every redirect URI in production. Keep refresh tokens and client secrets only on servers you control. Next Redirect URIs and callbacks /docs/accounts sign in/web/redirect uris — tighten registration and avoid mismatch errors. Sessions, cookies, and tokens /docs/accounts sign in/web/sessions and cookies — how Intastellar and your app set cookies such as inta acc and inta state .

title: Server-side (confidential) clients
description: Exchange the authorization code on your server with client_id and client_secret for Intastellar Accounts web sign-in.
text: Server-side (confidential) clients Exchange the authorization code on your server with client_id and client_secret for Intastellar Accounts web sign-in. When you have a trusted server Node, .NET, PHP, etc. , perform the token exchange there so the client secret never reaches the browser. Sequence 1. Browser completes the redirect flow and lands on your callback with code and state . 2. Your callback route verifies state , then calls your backend or runs server side in the same request to exchange the code. 3. Backend POST s to TOKEN ENDPOINT with grant type=authorization code , code , redirect uri , client id , and client secret . 4. Backend creates a session for the user set cookie, store tokens server side . 5. Browser is redirected to the app with only your session cookie. Example conceptual Add PKCE parameters if this client is configured as hybrid or if the authorization step used PKCE. Secret storage Load client secret from environment variables or a secret manager. Rotate secrets if exposed; use separate credentials per environment. Next Logout, errors, and troubleshooting /docs/accounts sign in/web/logout and errors .

title: Web sign-in — Getting started
description: Register your application, choose a client type, and plan redirects and sessions for Intastellar Accounts web sign-in.
text: Web sign-in — Getting started Register your application, choose a client type, and plan redirects and sessions for Intastellar Accounts web sign-in. Before you call any endpoint, configure an OAuth/OIDC style client for your product in the Intastellar developer console or equivalent registration UI your team uses . 1. Register your application Create an application record and capture: Client ID — public identifier for your app safe to ship in front end code for public clients . Client secret — only for confidential server side clients; never expose in the browser or mobile app binaries. Redirect URIs — exact HTTPS URLs where Intastellar may return the user after sign in. See Redirect URIs and callbacks /docs/accounts sign in/web/redirect uris . Use separate client registrations for production and staging so redirect URIs and secrets stay isolated. 2. Choose a flow Your app Recommended approach Single page app React, Vue, etc. Authorization code with PKCE ; no client secret in the browser. Server rendered site session cookies Code flow: browser completes the redirect; your server exchanges the code using the client secret. Mobile / native Same ideas as SPA: PKCE, custom URL scheme or HTTPS redirect. Details: Authorization code flow /docs/accounts sign in/web/authorization code flow , SPAs and JavaScript /docs/accounts sign in/web/spa and javascript , Server side exchange /docs/accounts sign in/web/backend exchange . 3. Endpoints and metadata Your console should list or you obtain from discovery : Authorization endpoint — user is sent here to sign in and approve scopes. Token endpoint — your backend or a secure BFF exchanges the code for tokens. Issuer / JWKS — for validating ID tokens when you use OpenID Connect. Placeholders in examples on this site are written as AUTHORIZATION ENDPOINT and TOKEN ENDPOINT ; substitute the values from your environment. 4. Plan sessions Decide how your site remembers the user after sign in: HTTP only, Secure cookies set by your server recommended for traditional web apps . Backend session with only an opaque session id in the cookie. Short lived access token in memory for SPAs, with refresh via a backend for frontend when possible. See Sessions, cookies, and tokens /docs/accounts sign in/web/sessions and cookies . Next steps Continue with Authorization code flow /docs/accounts sign in/web/authorization code flow to implement the first redirect and callback.

title: Logout, errors, and troubleshooting
description: End Intastellar Accounts sessions safely and interpret common OAuth errors from authorize and token endpoints.
text: Logout, errors, and troubleshooting End Intastellar Accounts sessions safely and interpret common OAuth errors from authorize and token endpoints. Logout 1. Clear your session — delete or invalidate your application session cookie and server side session record. 2. IdP logout optional but recommended — if Intastellar provides an end session or logout URL, redirect the user there with parameters specified in your integration guide id token hint , post logout redirect uri , client id , etc. so SSO cookies on the identity domain are cleared. 3. Return URL — send the user to a public page on your site after logout completes. Without step 2, the user may still be signed in to Intastellar and get a silent SSO on the next authorize redirect. Common authorize errors error typical Meaning invalid request Missing or invalid parameter e.g. bad redirect uri . unauthorized client Client not allowed for this flow or scope. access denied User cancelled or blocked consent. invalid scope Requested scope not allowed for the client. Always show a safe message to the user and log error description server side for support. Common token errors error Meaning invalid grant Code expired, already used, or redirect uri / PKCE mismatch. invalid client Wrong client id / client secret . invalid request Malformed body or missing field. Authorization codes are usually single use and short lived. If the user double submits the callback or you retry with the same code, expect invalid grant . Troubleshooting checklist Redirect URI /docs/accounts sign in/web/redirect uris matches the registered value exactly scheme, host, path, no extra query . state matches the value you stored for this attempt. PKCE: same code verifier that produced the sent code challenge . Clock skew: ensure server time is correct for JWT exp validation. CORS: token endpoint calls from the browser often fail by design — use your backend. For a full walkthrough of the happy path, see Authorization code flow /docs/accounts sign in/web/authorization code flow .

title: Redirect URIs and callbacks
description: Register exact callback URLs for Intastellar Accounts web sign-in and avoid common redirect mismatch errors.
text: Redirect URIs and callbacks Register exact callback URLs for Intastellar Accounts web sign-in and avoid common redirect mismatch errors. Intastellar only redirects to pre registered URLs. A typo, wrong scheme, or trailing slash mismatch causes redirect uri mismatch or similar errors. Rules of thumb 1. HTTPS in production — http://localhost is often allowed for development; production should use https:// . 2. Exact match — https://app.example.com/callback and https://app.example.com/callback/ are different paths; register the one you use in the authorize request. 3. No wildcards in most setups — register each concrete callback path or follow your console’s documented pattern if path templates are supported . 4. Query strings — avoid putting dynamic query strings in the registered URI unless your registration explicitly allows it; prefer a fixed path and pass internal context via state . Multiple environments Register separate redirect URIs or separate clients for: Local development http://127.0.0.1:5173/auth/callback , etc. Staging Production This limits blast radius if a secret leaks in a non production client. SPA routers If you use hash routing / /callback , check whether your identity provider allows that pattern for redirects; many require path based URLs /auth/callback for the OAuth callback. After redirect On the callback route: 1. Read code and state from the query string. 2. Verify state against what you stored when you started the flow. 3. Exchange the code at the token endpoint see Authorization code flow /docs/accounts sign in/web/authorization code flow . 4. Redirect the user to the final in app destination dashboard, return URL stored in state , etc. . Next Sessions, cookies, and tokens /docs/accounts sign in/web/sessions and cookies for how to persist the signed in user safely after a successful callback.

title: Sessions, cookies, and tokens
description: How Intastellar Accounts uses cookies such as inta_acc and inta_state, and how to combine them with your own session model.
text: Sessions, cookies, and tokens How Intastellar Accounts uses cookies such as inta_acc and inta_state, and how to combine them with your own session model. After a successful sign in you may see Intastellar set cookies on domains used by the Accounts / identity experience. On developers.intastellarsolutions.com , privacy disclosures reference cookies including: Cookie examples Typical role inta acc Session related token for the Accounts experience. inta state State for the sign in / consent flow. Exact behavior can evolve with the identity product; treat these as Intastellar managed cookies on Intastellar controlled hosts. Your integration should not depend on reading Intastellar cookies from your own origin unless documentation explicitly says you can. Your application session For your site app.example.com , prefer: 1. Your own session cookie — opaque session ID, HttpOnly , Secure , SameSite appropriate for your topology Lax or Strict for same site; None only with Secure if you must cross sites . 2. Server side session store — map session id to user id, token expiry, and refresh handling. 3. Short lived access token in memory SPA — paired with a BFF or silent refresh pattern; avoid long lived tokens in localStorage when possible. ID token vs access token ID token — JWT about the authentication event; use to establish who signed in; validate signature and claims iss , aud , exp , nonce if used . Access token — call Intastellar or resource APIs; treat as opaque unless you need to parse it. Logout Clear your session cookie and, if required by your product policy, redirect the user through Intastellar’s end session or logout endpoint so IdP cookies are cleared. See Logout, errors, and troubleshooting /docs/accounts sign in/web/logout and errors . Next SPAs and JavaScript clients /docs/accounts sign in/web/spa and javascript — PKCE and front end constraints. Server side confidential clients /docs/accounts sign in/web/backend exchange — exchanging the code without exposing secrets.

title: SPAs and JavaScript clients
description: Use PKCE without a client secret, protect tokens in the browser, and avoid common SPA pitfalls with Intastellar Accounts.
text: SPAs and JavaScript clients Use PKCE without a client secret, protect tokens in the browser, and avoid common SPA pitfalls with Intastellar Accounts. Single page applications cannot safely store a client secret . Use the authorization code flow with PKCE only. Flow summary 1. Generate code verifier high entropy random string and derive code challenge S256 . 2. Store code verifier where you can read it on callback — e.g. sessionStorage for the tab, or an encrypted cookie via a small BFF. 3. Redirect to AUTHORIZATION ENDPOINT with code challenge / code challenge method=S256 . 4. On callback, send code + code verifier to your backend recommended or to the token endpoint if the product allows public clients without a secret confirm in console . Prefer a backend for frontend BFF Even in a SPA, the token exchange and refresh are safer on a same origin API: Browser receives only an opaque session cookie from your API. Refresh tokens never touch localStorage . CORS and CSRF can be controlled on your domain. If you must handle tokens entirely in the browser, minimize lifetime, avoid localStorage for refresh tokens, and plan for XSS as a full compromise of the session. CORS and iframes Do not embed the Intastellar login UI in a hidden iframe unless the product explicitly supports silent or embedded flows. Prefer full page redirect for sign in and sign out. Next Server side confidential clients /docs/accounts sign in/web/backend exchange if you also serve a traditional backend.

title: Google Tag Manager
description: Load Intastellar Consents through Google Tag Manager.
text: Google Tag Manager Load Intastellar Consents through Google Tag Manager. Google Tag Manager Use GTM to inject the same bootstrap you would add in HTML by hand. 1. Create a Custom HTML tag with the window.INTA block and uc.js script from Get Started JavaScript /docs/cookie banner/javascript/getting started . 2. Fire it on Consent Initialization – All pages or your container’s equivalent so the banner loads before analytics and ads. 3. Add other tags with triggers that run only after consent state is available from Intastellar Consents—do not race the banner. ← Documentation home /docs/cookie banner

title: Intastellar Consents
description: Integrate Intastellar Consents (GDPR cookie banner) via JavaScript, WordPress, GTM, or Shopify.
text: Intastellar Consents Integrate Intastellar Consents (GDPR cookie banner) via JavaScript, WordPress, GTM, or Shopify. Documentation Intastellar Consents is a lightweight cookie banner you can drop in with a short script or WordPress plugin. It is built for GDPR aligned consent: block non essential cookies until the visitor chooses, then respect that choice across your stack. Use these guides to implement it on your own site. WordPress: latest packaged build v3.3.9 — Download plugin ZIP https://doc.intastellarsolutions.com/files/wordpress/gdpr/3.3.9/intastellar consents.zip . Implemented by

title: Customize
description: Tune colours, layout, language direction, and branding for the JavaScript banner.
text: Customize Tune colours, layout, language direction, and branding for the JavaScript banner. Customize The JavaScript banner reads configuration from window.INTA before uc.js runs. See the full JSON Schema reference /docs/cookie banner/javascript/inta schema . Common settings fields see Get Started /docs/cookie banner/javascript/getting started include: Field Purpose rootDomain Your site’s root domain company Display name for your organisation arrange Layout direction, e.g. ltr color Primary UI colour hex logo Absolute URL to your logo image design Banner presentation, e.g. overlay gtagId Google tag / GA4 measurement ID when applicable requiredCookies Cookies treated as strictly necessary keepInLocalStorage Local storage keys to preserve Add or adjust fields as documented for your account. For a fully custom UI, keep the script and apply the documented CSS classes to your markup see Can I use my own design? /docs/cookie banner can i use my own design on the docs home .

title: Get Started
description: Integrate Intastellar Consents on your website via JavaScript.
text: Get Started Integrate Intastellar Consents on your website via JavaScript. Get Started JavaScript Paste the snippet immediately after the opening <head tag on each page or once in your root layout . The same shape of config is shown on the public Intastellar Consents https://www.intastellarsolutions.com/solutions/cookie consents overview—swap in your real domains, IDs, and branding. Replace placeholders with your domain, company name, colours, logo URL, and measurement IDs. Privacy policy URL Set a reachable privacy policy URL. Use policy link and/or settings.privacy policy on window.INTA . Missing or invalid URLs are a common reason the banner stays hidden—see the FAQ /docs/cookie banner faq on the docs home. Related window.INTA reference JSON Schema /docs/cookie banner/javascript/inta schema Customize /docs/cookie banner/javascript/customize iFrames /docs/cookie banner/javascript/iframes Add logo /docs/cookie banner/javascript/logo Try out /docs/cookie banner/javascript/try out

title: iFrames
description: Consent-aware patterns when embedding third parties in iframes.
text: iFrames Consent-aware patterns when embedding third parties in iframes. iFrames Third party <iframe widgets players, maps, chat should only load once the matching purpose is allowed—same rules as scripts on the top level page. Wire iframe loading to your Intastellar Consents categories and each vendor’s docs. The overview on the documentation home /docs/cookie banner still applies: initialise the banner early, keep non essential requests blocked until consent, then enable embeds when appropriate.

title: INTA reference
description: JSON Schema for the window.INTA configuration object (JavaScript integration).
text: INTA reference JSON Schema for the window.INTA configuration object (JavaScript integration). window.INTA JSON Schema window.INTA is the global JavaScript object Intastellar Consents reads before uc.js runs. Define it in an inline <script in <head , then load the CDN script see Get Started /docs/cookie banner/javascript/getting started . Machine readable schema JSON Schema file: /schemas/window inta.json /schemas/window inta.json $id : https://inta.dev/schemas/window inta.json Use it with editors, validators, or codegen tools that support JSON Schema Draft 2020 12. Shape summary Path Type Notes policy link string URI Privacy policy URL settings object Banner UI and behaviour settings.rootDomain string Root domain settings.company string Display name settings.arrange "ltr" \ "rtl" Layout direction settings.color string Primary colour e.g. hex settings.logo string URI Logo URL settings.design string e.g. overlay settings.gtagId string Google / GA4 ID when applicable settings.privacy policy string URI Privacy URL often required for the banner to show settings.requiredCookies string Strictly necessary cookies settings.keepInLocalStorage string localStorage keys to keep The schema sets additionalProperties: true on the root and on settings , so extra keys your account or version expects are still valid—validate in your pipeline if you need a closed world. Example For field semantics beyond this reference, see Customize /docs/cookie banner/javascript/customize and the documentation home /docs/cookie banner .

title: Add logo
description: Add your logo to the WordPress cookie banner.
text: Add logo Add your logo to the WordPress cookie banner. Add logo WordPress Upload or select your logo in the WordPress plugin settings where branding is configured plugin UI labels may say Logo or similar . Use a clear PNG or SVG with reasonable dimensions for both desktop and mobile.
